scope: DirectDownloader.kt redirects, credential forwarding, cleartext downgrade and representation rebinding
Safety.kt and NetworkSettings.kt production network boundary
HttpRepresentation.kt, ResumeJournal.kt and ParallelDownloader.kt supporting representation checks
DirectDownloaderTest.kt, LiteralNetworkBoundaryTest.kt and SecurityReviewTest.kt existing coverage
positive_observations: Redirects are manual, bounded to six requests, and each destination is revalidated with Safety.url and requirePublicLiteral. The production client disables automatic redirects and HTTP proxies and validates DNS answers.

HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects are rejected before following the Location, independently of the opt-in cleartext preference. The production client separately denies initial HTTP requests when the preference is disabled.

Each redirect constructs a fresh request containing only the fixed user agent, identity encoding and optional range validators. Production client construction supplies no Authorization, Cookie, cookie jar or authenticator. User-info URLs, including user-info in redirect targets, are rejected by Safety.url.

A resumed 206 must match both the final target URL hash and strong ETag before opening the output, and its range total and endpoints must agree with the durable checkpoint. A full 200 replaces the previous bytes. Parallel ranges likewise bind the final URL and validator.
test_gaps: Existing source tests do not explicitly cover a cross-origin redirect chain with credentials in Location, followed by an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade while cleartext is enabled.

Existing direct resume tests cover changed validators and source URLs but lack an explicit redirect that changes the final target while reusing the same ETag and matching Content-Range; source inspection shows the target hash rejects that 206 before mutation.
runtime_execution: Read-only static review only. No builds, test execution, devices or publishing. Test-only injected transports were not classified as production security bypasses.
